blockers.title: The artifact exports DR-101's own decision-column fragment 'signing/notarization' to DR-112 and DR-110, which do not own it — orphaning the obligation between rows
blockers.subjectQuote: standing: 'RESERVED. Signing ROLES are listed. Ceremony/thresholds/notarization ride DR-112 / DR-110 / platform owners.' owner: 'DR-112 / DR-110 / platform-release owners'. signingRolesNote: 'Ceremony, thresholds, notarization are OD-101-2 / DR-112 / DR-110.'

measurement.whereNotarizationActuallyLives: I searched every file under docs/v2/ and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md for 'notariz'. In file 08 it occurs exactly once, in the DR-101 decision column at line 283: 'Native signed distribution-core language, mandatory closure/TCB inventory, layering, signing/notarization, platforms'. It occurs zero times in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
measurement.whatDR112ActuallyOwns: File 08 line 294: 'Signed-index refresh, expiry, last-known revocation, quorum loss, root recovery, emergency running-component policy'. Its evidence cell's 'recovery ceremony' is root-key recovery for the signed index. Neither core code-signing nor OS notarization appears.
measurement.whatDR110ActuallyOwns: File 08 line 292: 'Core self-update/repair/rollback and repair-media trust', evidence 'Signed clean-machine repair, crash injection, revocation-aware rollback, removable-media/expiry tests'. Neither core code-signing nor OS notarization appears.
measurement.theOneSourceThatDoesPairNotarizationWith: File 02 lines 248-250: 'Exact packaging, signing, notarization, exception, and platform mechanics remain owned decisions under DR-119 and gate DR-G14.' That sentence is scoped to the self-contained LANGUAGE-RUNTIME rule (the Node packaging case at lines 246-248) — a subject this very artifact removes from the default install at /defaultInstall/excludes[0] 'language runtimes' and parks at ID-DEP-K4. So the only warrant in the corpus for moving notarization off DR-101 is scoped to a subject the artifact itself excludes, and it names DR-119/DR-G14 — not the DR-112/DR-110 the artifact names.
measurement.netResult: No row other than DR-101 carries core signing or OS notarization. I also scanned every DR-1xx row for sign/trust language to be sure I was not missing an owner; DR-103's 'delegated roles, IDs, provenance/SBOM/attestation binding' is manifest-signing identity, which supports the artifact's ROLE LIST but not a ceremony owner.

blockers.whyThisIsABlockerAndNotAShouldFix: It is a false ownership assignment for a decision-column fragment of the row under review, and it is load-bearing for that row's closure. If recorded, DR-101's decision column reads as fully dispositioned — inventory answered, language reserved to a later DR-101 successor, notarization owned elsewhere — while in fact no row owns core signing/notarization. A later SATISFIED argument for DR-101 could cite 'notarization rides DR-112 / DR-110' against two rows that will never discharge it, and each of those rows would correctly disclaim it as out of its own decision column. That is register corruption by construction, and it is the authority-migration failure this artifact elsewhere works hard to prevent.
blockers.theArtifactsOwnStandardRefutesIt: OD-101-1 handles the sibling reservation correctly: owner is 'A later Route-C or rule-governed successor, not this extraction' — the obligation stays in DR-101's lane and is merely deferred in time. OD-101-2 breaks that pattern by deferring in ROW instead. The asymmetry is unexplained, and OBL-D2's own standing ('ceremony/notarization RESERVED') is inconsistent with an owner field that hands the fragment to other rows.
blockers.charitableReadingIConsideredAndRejected: OD-101-2 could be read as naming DR-112/DR-110 merely as suppliers of adjacent ceremony mechanics while DR-101 retains the decision. I rejected that reading because the field is literally named 'owner', because signingRolesNote states the flat proposition 'Ceremony, thresholds, notarization ARE OD-101-2 / DR-112 / DR-110', and because OD-101-1 shows the author knows how to write a same-row reservation when that is what is meant. If the coordinator adopts the charitable reading, this drops to SHOULD-FIX — the wording still needs repair either way.
blockers.minimumRepair: Set OD-101-2.owner to a later DR-101 successor, mirroring OD-101-1's form. Restate DR-112/DR-110 as adjacent or input mechanics rather than owners, and drop the 'are' in signingRolesNote. If the author does believe another row owns core notarization, quote the row text that says so; on the live bytes no such text exists.

verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 4 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. The dispatch gate was ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: The extraction discipline here is strong and I could not break it where the dispatch pointed me: the row quote and the 30 carried lines are byte-exact, the stale file 02 sentence is named rather than repeated, the three cores stay uncollapsed, no core language is minted, DR-106 storage stays out of the default install, and nothing is marked SATISFIED or QUALIFIED. The candidate fails on something the dispatch did not name. In reserving the decision-column fragment 'signing/notarization' it does not defer the fragment in TIME to a later DR-101 successor, as it correctly does for language; it defers it in ROW, to DR-112 and DR-110. Neither row carries core signing or OS notarization in its decision column, and 'notariz' appears in file 08 exactly once — in DR-101's own row. The obligation would be orphaned between rows, which is the authority migration this artifact was otherwise built to prevent. Four SHOULD-FIX items follow from the same family of quiet loosening: a source sentence reproduced with 'current' deleted, restatement fields that strip every proposal hedge the verbatim block preserves, a decision-column decomposition covering three of five fragments, and a D-056 role line that understates how far this row sits from eligibility on the artifact's own reservations. None of the four is fatal alone; together with B-1 they describe a candidate whose verbatim layer is disciplined and whose restatement layer is not.
coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-101 stays OPEN at file 08 line 283; I edited nothing but this file, committed nothing, and read no other reviewer of this subject. B-1 is repairable in a v2 without reopening the extraction: the verbatim layer, the platform set, the three-core separation and the DR-106 exclusion all survived attack and should carry forward unchanged. The one judgement call I want visible is B-1's severity — I graded it a blocker because it misassigns ownership of a fragment of the reviewed row's own decision column, but a coordinator who reads OD-101-2's 'owner' field as naming input suppliers rather than deciders can fairly downgrade it to SHOULD-FIX. The verdict is unchanged either way, since four SHOULD-FIX items stand independently. One caution for whoever dispositions this: ADV-1 means the artifact's COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin no longer resolves, so re-verify against live bytes rather than the recorded digest.
